 EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

The Government of Turkmenistan (GoT) and the United Nations Country Team (UNCT) in Turkmenistan
are pleased to present the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (CF) for
2026-2030.
This CF was developed as a result of a national consultative process. It ensures consistency between the
national development strategies and priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). It provides
a frame for the alignment of efforts of UNCT in Turkmenistan, the GoT and other development partners in
supporting growth opportunities and helping to address the main development challenges confronting the
country and fulfilling international human rights obligations of Turkmenistan.
This document outlines how the UNCT will work together with the GoT and other stakeholders intending
to support Turkmenistan in maximising its potential for achieving the SDGs based on the country’s human
and natural resources, commitment and the will of its government and development opportunities.
Building on previous cooperation, UNCT in Turkmenistan is committed to support further the GoT in its
journey towards sustainable development that leaves no one behind, based on mutually agreed priorities.
The UN development team will work in close collaboration with the GoT and assist in the process of policy
design and implementation, data collection and analysis required for sustainable development.
The country is progressing towards the SDGs, although growth opportunities and development challenges
related to the governance system and economic transformation, environment and climate change, and social
development remain. National development programs of Turkmenistan are aimed at addressing these
challenges.
The CF builds on the joint SDG gaps analysis conducted in the framework of the Common Country
Analysis by the UNCT and the GoT for the main SDG transitions with high potential for systemic impact:
food security and water management, green energy transition, digital connectivity, education, jobs and
social protection, climate change, biodiversity loss and pollution, universal health coverage, and peace and
security.
The CF reaffirms the shared vision and partnership between the GoT and the UN system. It expresses joint
aspirations for a prosperous, inclusive, and resilient Turkmenistan, and envisions that the country, by 2030,
will make significant progress in achieving its national development goals aligned with the SDGs with the
UN support within the following three strategic priorities:
       A. Good Governance and Inclusive and Diversified Economic Growth
       B. Environment and Climate Change Mitigation and Adaptation
       C. Equitable Social Development and Well-being
These priorities are fully in line with the long-term socio-economic policy of Turkmenistan set in the
Programme “The Revival in the New Epoch of the Powerful State: National Programme of Socio-
Economic Development of Turkmenistan in 2022–2052”, “The Programme of the President of
Turkmenistan for the socio-economic development of the country in 2022–2028”, new edition of
“National Programme of the President of Turkmenistan for the Transformation of Social and Living
Conditions of the Population of Villages, Towns, Etrap Cities and Etrap Centres for the period up to 2028”
and other national programmes, that are aimed at ensuring sustainable economic development, consistent
improvement of the public administration system, increasing social protection of the population, further
improving wellbeing, and a prosperous and happy life of the population.
To accelerate the achievement of the SDGs along the national priorities, the UN system in Turkmenistan
will leverage its role as a convenor of diverse stakeholders, an advisor on development, a promoter of
                                                   v
 international human rights obligations and best practices and an advocate for leaving no one behind.
Cooperation between the UN system organizations and the Government of Turkmenistan will evolve
around four expected outcomes:
Outcome A1. By 2030, the people of Turkmenistan have access to accountable governance system
through improved public administration and strengthened fiscal capacity, based on commitments to
human rights, rule of law and gender equality
Outcome A2. By 2030, Turkmenistan will have improved conditions and opportunities for inclusive
and sustainable economic diversification and growth
Outcome B1. By 2030, Turkmenistan will strengthen natural resource management systems,
systematically fulfil its climate change commitments, and the population will become more resilient
to climate change and disasters
Outcome C1. By 2030, all people of Turkmenistan, including vulnerable groups, benefit equitably
from quality and inclusive health, education and social protection systems and transformative social
norms
The integrated nature of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development interlinks strategic priorities and
outcomes. Together with human rights and gender equality, they embody a nexus of change with progress
under each outcome requiring and contributing to the progress of other priority areas.
These strategic priorities and outcomes were developed considering the broader Central Asia, cross-border
and Caspian littoral states context. The UN system will support Turkmenistan in its engagement with
neighbouring countries to address common development challenges and growth opportunities, including
through forming strategic partnerships with regional and sub-regional development institutions.
Under this CF, the UNCT configuration is tailored to focus on building sustainable national institutional
and financial capacities to coordinate and deliver the SDG agenda, strengthening capacity and systems,
scaling up successful development approaches, empowering youth and mainstreaming the Leave No One
Behind principle into national policies and practices.
This CF places emphasis on joint ownership, stronger UN presence, coordinated and joint programming,
most effective use of available resources, increasing involvement in regional cooperation initiatives and
strengthened engagement with IFIs, and greater involvement of the private sector and civil society.
Integrated, cross-sectoral and system-strengthening approaches promoted by the CF should increase
chances of success and leverage to achieve wider downstream benefits, especially for the most vulnerable
groups.
In line with the UN’s commitment to national ownership, implementation of the CF will involve mutual
accountability and joint Government-UN system mechanisms for the effective coordination and
implementation of the cooperation. Joint Government-UN oversight will be formally exercised by a
Steering Committee, while Results Groups established in line with the four outcomes, will allow for
improved coordination and joint programming. The annual UN Country Results Report will be the key
document used by the Steering Committee to review progress, identify resource gaps and foster stronger
partnerships to achieve the Cooperation Framework targets by 2030.
The CF 2026-2030 for Turkmenistan represents a comprehensive approach to sustainable development,
aligning national priorities with global goals. Through collaborative efforts, the GoT and UN aim to create
a more prosperous, equitable, and resilient society for all people.

    CHAPTER 1: COUNTRY CONTEXT AND PROGRESS TOWARD AGENDA 2030

   1.1 Development Context
1. Governance. According to the Constitution Turkmenistan is a democratic, legal and secular state in which
   state governance is carried out in the form of a presidential republic. State power in Turkmenistan is divided
   into legislative (Mejlis of Turkmenistan (Parliament)), executive (Cabinet of Ministers of Turkmenistan)
   and judicial powers, which act independently, balancing each other. Following independence in 1991,
   Turkmenistan adopted a gradual approach to economic and political reforms with the state playing a leading
   role in the economy.
2. Population. Turkmenistan is a country with a rapid demographic growth. Its 7,057,841 population is
   projected to increase by some 30% by 2050.2 Desert covers most of the country, concentrating the sparse
   population in a few urban areas (47.1% of population is urban). The country is young, with a median age
   of 28,7 years and 34.9% of population are children.
3. Human rights. The authorities in Turkmenistan believe that using UN platforms to discuss and act on
   human rights is the best approach and they engage various UN human rights mechanisms. There are tangible
   improvements in the capacities of the Office of Ombudsperson and some advancement in the gender
   equality agenda. Next years will be critical to further advance the implementation of the GoT’s
   commitments in the area of human rights with the support of the UN system.
4. Economy. Turkmenistan is a landlocked upper-middle-income country. Steady economic growth driven
   over the past two decades has been supported by favourable global energy prices. This led to an increase in
   country’s Human Development Index from 0.71 (108th globally) in 2018 to 0.74 (94th) in 20243. However,
   dependence on the hydrocarbon sector, makes the economy vulnerable to external shocks. Building a
   resilient and diversified economy should become a key policy priority in Turkmenistan. The agricultural
   sector, which is crucial for domestic consumption, is reliant on water-intensive crops (cotton, wheat, rice).
   Private sector development has significant potential to grow. Ensuring macroeconomic stability, structural
   reforms, enhanced business climate and increasing role of the private sector in the economy is expected to
   have a positive effect on investments, both domestic and foreign. It will allow enabling economic
   transformation through structural changes and raising within-sector productivity growth, increasing
   manufacturing sector’s value added, addressing informal economy and thus generating higher tax revenues.
   Higher labour force participation and formal employment, including among youth and women, are
   important aspects of demographic resilience. Turkmenistan has a vast potential to maintain its low public
   debt levels through enhancements in revenue collection, while substantially increasing its spending in the
   social sector compared to Upper Middle Income Countries’ average benchmarks. Increasing effectiveness
   of the monetary policy is linked to the development of the banking sector and deepening of the financial
   market. Thus, inclusive diversification, economic restructuring and private sector development are key
   policy priorities, calling for a highly skilled workforce, accelerated structural reforms and transition towards
   the inclusive and diversified market economy.
5. Integration into regional and global economy. For a landlocked country which is in the process of WTO
   accession, improving transport connectivity is crucial for expanding Turkmenistan’s trade and economic
   growth. Turkmenistan has a potential to enhance its logistics capacity and transportation infrastructure,
   considering its strategic location at the heart of Central Asia. Developing agri-food systems and improving
   food security alongside water management in Turkmenistan can catalyse significant economic
   transformation and job creation, while also fostering systemic impacts across multiple SDGs. The economic

    policy of Turkmenistan is aimed at ensuring sustainable economic growth, diversifying the national
   economy, its transition to an industrial and innovative development path, increasing competitiveness and
   moving towards the development of processing sectors that produce high value-added products, including
   in the hydrocarbon sector. The peace-energy nexus is important, as Turkmenistan is a critical supplier of
   electricity to Afghanistan. Improving energy connectivity and methane emission reduction are linked to the
   upgrade of energy infrastructure, reduction of technological losses and regional cooperation. Carbon
   neutrality will require a shift in the allocation of investment in the future energy systems across all low-
   and zero-carbon technologies.
6. Environment. Turkmenistan has demonstrated its commitment to climate change mitigation, and further
   progress will depend on decreasing reliance on fossil fuels. The country’s vast renewable energy potential,
   particularly solar and wind, will play a key role in just energy transition, replacing fossil fuels as the main
   source of energy in the economy. The energy sector, in particular the gas industry, plays an important role
   in supporting Turkmenistan’s development, including through the promotion of energy-efficient
   technologies in production processes and initiatives to reduce methane emissions. Smart agriculture and
   circular economy solutions can be further advanced. Water scarcity remains a critical environmental
   challenge, along with improvements in irrigation infrastructure, increasing water management efficiency,
   as well as reduction of use of chemical fertilisers and pesticides in agriculture and their impact on soil and
   water contamination. New and heightened climate-induced risks are emerging, while the population of
   Turkmenistan, similar to other countries in the region, is highly vulnerable to the effects of climate change.
   Turkmenistan, therefore, initiated the establishment of the Regional Centre for Climate Technology for
   Central Asia (RCCTCA) in Turkmenistan, which was supported by all Central Asian states. UNCT
   expressed full support for this initiative and engaged in negotiations with key stakeholders. The Centre will
   serve as a climate technology transfer mechanism and knowledge hub for the region's countries. It will
   provide countries with tailored country-specific technical and advisory support on climate technology-
   related issues.
7. Social development. Turkmenistan is a socially-oriented state which aims to demonstrate the links between
   the country’s economic growth and the wellbeing of its population, considering equity and living standards
   of its population in the rural areas. The government is committed to allocate at least 70 percent of the state
   budget expenditure to the social sector, including health, education, social protection, culture and housing,
   which can still be increased as a percentage of GDP. The social protection system in Turkmenistan is a
   state-run framework that provides material support (both monetary and non-monetary) as well as social
   services. It offers an extensive safety net for most citizens and newly established inclusive community-
   based social services.
   Turkmenistan has achieved universal primary school enrolment and needs to address regional and gender
   disparities in access to education, as well as increase pre-school enrolment. In the health sector, access to
   health assistance at childbirth is almost universal, as is coverage of children with preventive vaccinations.
   Among the pending priorities is reduction of the child mortality rate and related rates of neonatal and infant
   mortality from preventable causes, as well as promoting exclusive breastfeeding. The country has made
   substantial efforts in bringing down the incidences of key communicable diseases as well as tobacco and
   alcohol consumption. To advance social development, a balanced approach to public expenditures is needed
   between infrastructural investments and investments in human capital and structural adjustments, including
   the expansion of the national model of inclusive community-based social services. Health risks are still
   higher in rural areas due to deficient access to safe drinking water and health services. Turkmenistan shows
   progress toward national nutrition targets, such as reduction of anaemia among children and women, salt
   iodization and flour fortification, however, further acceleration of targeted interventions is required as
   outlined in the Turkmenistan National Micronutrient Survey 2024.4

 8. Leave No One Behind. Effectiveness of addressing the needs of those left behind in Turkmenistan should
   increase through improved access to disaggregated data. According to the recent CCA, these groups mainly
   include5:
  - Women and girls. Attention to women and children rights is increasing in the context of building
    demographic resilience. The legal framework protecting the rights of women and girls is in place and
    needs steady implementation across various domains. Significant progress has been made in addressing
    women’s reproductive health and access to health services, although the access is not yet equal. A lower
    education level considerably reduces women’s chances for jobs and livelihood opportunities.
    Addressing gender-based violence requires legislative changes and a comprehensive preventive
    strategy.
  - Children and young people. As more than one third of country’s population is youth, improving youth
    policies based on reliable data is high on the GoT’s agenda. Access of youth to formal compulsory
    school education is guaranteed, although young women’s enrolment in post-secondary education still
    needs to be increased, and opportunities for nonformal learning need to be expanded and diversified.
    Young people who are neither in employment nor in education or training are especially at risk of
    becoming socially disadvantaged. Youth rights awareness and engagement is increasing. The State
    Programme on Youth Policy outlines the need for youth-oriented social protection and its
    implementation needs to be secured in the coming years. The National Action Plan for Realisation of
    Children’s Rights in Turkmenistan for 2023-2028 is another important achievement to be enforced and
    monitored. Legislative and administrative measures should adequately protect the rights of children
    belonging to ethnic minorities, girls, children with disabilities and those living with multiple
    deprivations. Overcoming the existing digital divide and unequal use of technologies by young people,
    will enhance digital access in schools.
  - Persons with Disabilities. Different state and non-state actors are involved institutionally in the support
    system for persons with disabilities, mainly based on a medical model of service provision. A more
    comprehensive approach to support services, access to mainstream education for children with
    disabilities, developing inclusive community care, assistive technologies, specialised professional
    services for these groups and coverage with social assistance system are among the pending priorities.
    Further support will be needed to align national legislative and normative base with international
    standards, conduct transformative social and behaviour change initiatives, to reduce the risks of
    discrimination and violence, against persons with disabilities.
  - Refugees and stateless people. Turkmenistan has made substantial progress in the past decade to address
    and prevent statelessness within its borders, officially becoming the second country in the world to
    eradicate statelessness in 2024. With the support of international partners, policies towards recognising
    the rights of asylum-seekers and refugees needs to be developed.
  - People affected by migration. Turkmenistan has been consistently working for improvement of
    migration governance in the country and in this area it is important to strengthen systems of reintegration
    support for returning migrants in vulnerable situations and their families through a case management
    approach across economic, social and psychological dimensions, taking into account their specific
    needs, vulnerability, age, gender as well as skills and knowledge they acquired in migration.
  - Elderly people. The relatively small elderly population in Turkmenistan is traditionally treated with
    respect in society but public policies need to ensure that they do not experience social and economic
    vulnerabilities.

        - Groups at risk of STI, including HIV. Estimating numbers of people at risk of STI, including HIV, is
         challenging due to data availability and social stigma. Controlling the risk of STI growth is associated

       - Children without parental care. The Government emphasizes the importance of family-based care for
         children who, for various reasons, cannot live with their parents. At the same time, family-based care
         options for children without parental care are limited, with most state support focused on institutional
         care for children, especially for children with disabilities. As a result, there has been a steady increase
         in the number of children living in residential institutions, by approximately 4-5% per year. The National
         Action Plan for the Realisation of Children’s Rights in Turkmenistan for 2023-2028 aims to further
         develop the system of social services and family-based alternative care and child protection towards a
         rights- and community-based and preventive child protection.
       - People with substance use disorders. The drug policy in Turkmenistan is based on international treaties
         and guarantees universal access to social rights for people with high-risk behaviours. To prevent and
         reduce the use of new psychoactive substances and potent medications, it is necessary to raise public
         awareness about their harmful effects and the negative consequences of their use.


       1.2 National Development Vision
9.      Key national development frameworks. Turkmenistan is taking steps to nationalise and localise the
        SDGs through its national policies. The long-term national vision is guided by “The Revival in the New
        Epoch of the Powerful State: National Programme of Socio-Economic Development of Turkmenistan,
        2022–2052”, The Program of the President of Turkmenistan for the Socio-economic development of the
        country in 2022–2028 and new edition of the National Programme of the President of Turkmenistan for
        the Transformation of Social and Living Conditions of the Population of Villages, Towns, Etrap Cities
        and Etrap Centres for the period up to 2028.
10. “The Revival in the New Epoch of the Powerful State National Programme of Socio-Economic
    Development of Turkmenistan for 2022–2052” aims at the formation of a new model for the
    harmonious and sustainable development of the national economy of Turkmenistan through:
i)         Ensuring the political, economic, social and cultural development of the country;
ii)        Further strengthening of the foundations of national independence and neutrality in the next thirty
           years;
iii)       Improvement of the public administration system in accordance with the changing conditions of the
           market economy;
iv)        Strengthening macroeconomic stability;
v)         Improving the competitiveness of the national economy and strengthening its position at the level of
           sustainably developing countries of the world;
vi)        Increasing the level of industrialisation of the national economy, enhancing the implementation of
           institutional reforms, digital economy and digital technologies, active development of the market
           economy, small and medium-sized enterprises, creation of an enabling business environment;
vii)       Further development of economic sectors based on knowledge, innovations, including economically
           and environmentally friendly technologies;

ix)        Ensuring environmental and food security, promoting the development of the circular and “green
           economy”;
x)         Development of human capital, further improvement of living standards, social protection and
           employment of citizens;
xi)        Ensuring consistent implementation of the SDGs in Turkmenistan.

11. The Programme of the President of Turkmenistan for the Socio-Economic Development of the
    country in 2022–2028 aims at sustainable economic growth of the country, structural transformations
    of all sectors of the economy, creation of a robust infrastructure, expanding integration into the global
    economy , introduction of innovations and digital systems in all production areas, increasing the role of
    private businesses, achieving living standards on a par with advanced economies.
12. New edition of the Programme on Reforming the Living Conditions of Populations of Villages,
    Towns, Cities in Etraps and Etrap Centres. Through this Programme, which suggests strategies for
    regional and local level development , the GoT aims at the development of velayats (regions) through
    expanding the production of domestic products, increasing the income of the population, creating new
    jobs, improving infrastructure, upgrade and renovation of human settlements.


      1.3 Progress towards SDGs
13. National commitment to SDGs. In 2017, by the Decree of the President, the Ministry of Finance and
    Economy of Turkmenistan was appointed as the Coordinating body for SDG implementation, which
    ensured monitoring and coordination of the process of implementing SDGs at the national level. The
    responsibility for creating and maintaining an SDG database has been assigned to the State Committee
    of Statistics (SCS) of Turkmenistan, enabling the systematic monitoring of the progress of implementing
    the SDG targets and indicators adopted by the country and developing the necessary measures and
    policies in a timely manner. The main steps and actions taken by Turkmenistan to achieve the goals and
    objectives in the field of sustainable development were highlighted in the book of the National Leader
    of the Turkmen People “Turkmenistan is on the Way to Achieving the Sustainable Development Goals”,
    presented at the 73rd session of the UN General Assembly. The UN system supports the Rapid Integrated
    Assessment (RIA) process, which facilitates mainstreaming the SDGs into national policies and plans.
14. Recent progress in achieving SDGs. The GoT’s assessed its progress towards achieving SDGs through
    the Voluntary National Reviews of Turkmenistan conducted in 2019 and 2023. Since the presentation
    of the First Voluntary National Review, the GoT has been working on nationalisation of SDGs and
    streamlining the list of national SDG targets and indicators. As of 23 June 2022, 136 targets and 180
    indicators have been adopted in Turkmenistan for implementation until 2030. The second VNR proved
    that the level of incorporation of SDG targets into strategies, programmes and action plans is as high as
    85%.6 In particular, the review noted progress in the following areas: i) Applying a human-centred
    approach is at the core of the sustainable model of governance through public investments in social
    sphere; ii) Introduction of “green” technologies and climate change actions, including through the

    key priority for the UNCT entities, with a special focus on prioritizing victims' rights and creating an
    environment in which sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA) do not occur. SEA is unacceptable behaviour
    and is prohibited for UN personnel and UN implementing partners. The UNCT entities will therefore pursue
    all appropriate means to protect against, prevent and respond to SEA, and will require a similar commitment

    SEA, (iii) investigate allegations, and (iv) take appropriate corrective action when incidents occur, including
    providing support to victims in accordance with a victim centred approach.
